---
title: "Power: Minimum Detectable Effect of the Main Specification"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
  message: false
  warning: false
---

The design's main specification is a two-way fixed effects regression of `outcome` on
`treated` with unit and year effects and standard errors clustered by unit. This exploration
simulates the sampling distribution of that estimate under no effect and reports the minimum
detectable effect (MDE) at 80% power for a two-sided 5% test. Its result is copied into the
manuscript's `design.checks.power`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)

set.seed(20260908L)

# Simulated draws. Small, so the fixture renders quickly; the Monte Carlo error of the MDE is
# reported below.
N_DRAWS <- 200L
# The effect the design is built to detect: the synthetic panel's true effect
# (data/raw/data_manifest.md: "true ATT 0.30").
TARGET_EFFECT <- 0.30
POWER <- 0.80
TEST_LEVEL <- 0.05
```

```{r}
#| label: null-draws
panel <- read_csv(here("data/raw/panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# The main specification, fit once. Its residuals carry no treatment effect, and removing the
# estimated effect from its fitted values leaves the unit and year structure under no effect.
fit_main <- feols(outcome ~ treated | unit + year, data = panel, cluster = ~unit)
beta_main <- coef(fit_main)[["treated"]]
panel_null <- panel |>
  mutate(fitted_null = fitted(fit_main) - beta_main * treated, resid_null = resid(fit_main))
stopifnot("one fitted value per row" = nrow(panel_null) == nrow(panel))

# Each draw resamples whole units' residual paths (with replacement), so the within-unit
# correlation that clustering by unit allows for is kept.
unit_ids <- sort(unique(panel_null$unit))
draw_estimate <- function(draw_id) {
  donor_units <- sample(unit_ids, length(unit_ids), replace = TRUE)
  donor_resid <- panel_null |>
    select(donor = unit, year, resid_draw = resid_null)
  panel_draw <- tibble(unit = unit_ids, donor = donor_units) |>
    inner_join(panel_null, by = "unit", relationship = "one-to-many") |>
    inner_join(donor_resid, by = c("donor", "year")) |>
    mutate(outcome_draw = fitted_null + resid_draw)
  stopifnot("each draw keeps every unit-year" = nrow(panel_draw) == nrow(panel_null))
  fit_draw <- feols(outcome_draw ~ treated | unit + year, data = panel_draw, cluster = ~unit)
  tibble(draw = draw_id, estimate = coef(fit_draw)[["treated"]], std_error = se(fit_draw)[["treated"]])
}
null_draws <- map(seq_len(N_DRAWS), draw_estimate) |> list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: mde
null_sd <- sd(null_draws$estimate)
mde_multiplier <- qnorm(1 - TEST_LEVEL / 2) + qnorm(POWER)
mde <- mde_multiplier * null_sd
# Monte Carlo standard error of a standard deviation estimated from N_DRAWS draws.
mde_mc_se <- mde_multiplier * null_sd / sqrt(2 * (N_DRAWS - 1))
mean_clustered_se <- mean(null_draws$std_error)
```

## Result

Across `r N_DRAWS` null draws the estimate has standard deviation `r round(null_sd, 4)`
(mean clustered standard error `r round(mean_clustered_se, 4)`). The MDE at
`r round(100 * POWER)`% power for a two-sided `r round(100 * TEST_LEVEL)`% test is
**`r round(mde, 3)`** (Monte Carlo SE `r round(mde_mc_se, 3)`), against a target effect of
`r TARGET_EFFECT`.

Recorded in the manuscript's `design.checks.power`: mde `r round(mde, 3)`, target_effect
`r TARGET_EFFECT`, draws `r N_DRAWS`.
